hints.title: Repeated Tree Traversal Obstacle
hints.text: Running a separate traversal from every node takes quadratic time, timing out on trees with tens of thousands of nodes. When you shift the designated root to an adjacent neighbor, how do the path distances change for nodes inside that neighbor's subtree compared to nodes outside it?

hints.title: Subtree Shift Invariant
hints.text: Moving the root across an edge makes every node inside the neighbor's subtree one step closer and every other node one step farther; subtree sizes say how many nodes are on each side.

hints.title: Two-Pass Procedure and Recurrence
hints.text: Perform an iterative breadth-first search from node 0 to establish parent relationships and topological ordering. Process nodes in reverse topological order to accumulate subtree sizes count[i] and ans[0]. Then process nodes in forward topological order, updating ans[v] = ans[p] - count[v] + (n - count[v]) for each child v with parent p.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import deque

class Solution:
    def sumOfDistancesInTree(self, n: int, edges: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        if n <= 1:
            return [0]

        adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v in edges:
            adj[u].append(v)
            adj[v].append(u)

        parent = [-1] * n
        order = []
        visited = [False] * n
        visited[0] = True
        queue = deque([0])

        while queue:
            u = queue.popleft()
            order.append(u)
            for v in adj[u]:
                if not visited[v]:
                    visited[v] = True
                    parent[v] = u
                    queue.append(v)

        count = [1] * n
        ans = [0] * n

        for u in reversed(order[1:]):
            p = parent[u]
            count[p] += count[u]
            ans[p] += ans[u] + count[u]

        for u in order[1:]:
            p = parent[u]
            ans[u] = ans[p] - count[u] + (n - count[u])

        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Two-pass tree rerooting using iterative BFS ordering to support arbitrary tree depths without recursion limits.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Running an independent BFS or DFS traversal from every single node takes O(N^2) time. For N = 3 * 10^4, this requires (3 * 10^4)^2 = 9 * 10^8 operations, exceeding the 1-second timeout by an order of magnitude and risking deep recursion call stack overflow on skewed tree paths.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing O(N) auxiliary tree metadata (count[u] subtree node counts and ans[u] running distances) across two linear passes (O(N) time) computes all N tree distance sums with zero redundant traversals.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Deriving the rerooting transition formula ans[v] = ans[u] - count[v] + (n - count[v]) from first principles (moving root to child v brings its count[v] subtree nodes 1 step closer and moves the remaining n - count[v] nodes 1 step farther).
